summary: A candidate turns down an offer politely and says the other role fits their goals better.
realLife: Career guidance says to decline in writing, thank the employer and not say you got a better job; say the other role fits your goals at this stage. Backing out after accepting costs employers time and the candidate's reputation.
sources: UW-Madison SuccessWorks, accepting and negotiating your offer: https://successworks.wisc.edu/accepting-and-negotiating-your-offer/
inGame: Declining is a choice on the offer call; reputation carries on the person's ties to those at the employer. Needs: an offer record. Scene: needs a producer for job-offer.

turns.summary: The candidate says the other role pays far better and the employer takes offense.
turns.writesBack: The tie to the employer turns cold, and word may reach other employers.

turns.summary: The candidate never answers and lets the offer lapse.
turns.writesBack: The employer's trust falls, and a note is made in the journal.

turns.summary: The candidate declines kindly and offers to stay in touch for later roles.
pulledBy: a hiring manager with a good tie
turns.writesBack: The tie stays warm, and a promise to talk again is made.
